posts.topic_title: New holo 8 by 10 inch made with ATI laser
posts.author: Kris Meerlo
posts.post_subject: New holo 8 by 10 inch made with ATI laser
posts.content_md:
Some pictures made with the ATI laser.

-The laser is 35 mW and 655nm.

-Ultimate 15nm 8 by 10 inch plate.

-Exposure time 5 seconds.

-Use singlets for expanding beam ( Thanks Colin for the tip ).

-Halfwave plate.

-Denisyuke hologram thus single beam.

Yes I now I steal the idea of making a skull with a flower look at the backside of the book holography handbook.

posts.author: Kris Meerlo
posts.post_subject: New holo 8 by 10 inch made with ATI laser
posts.content_md:
I made this hologram with the laser from analogtechnologies.

 You can see in the skull hologram another statue about 40 cm deep ( 

 not in the pictures ) 

 In the beginning I have some problems with it but now with the new

 design ( I have made more then 25 holograms with it in 2 mounths )

 i think the laser is stable and suitable for holography.

 But the laser is sensitive for backreflection I think every laserdiode is 

 sensitive for back reflection.

 I use in the holo setup a live interfero test and can then check if there 

 are movements or onstable diode behaviour if there are not to much 

 back reflections then the laser is very stable and no mode hops.

 They bought also 2 holo's from me for showing it on the Photonic west 

 show and they place some holo pictures in their datasheet.

 They asked me also if there is much interest for their modehop free

 laserdiode, who consider to buy a laser from them?

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.post_subject: New holo 8 by 10 inch made with ATI laser
posts.content_md: I don't understand the reason, but I have noticed that the apparent depth of reflection holograms increases with their size. I think it's something like the intrinsic angular resolution being unchanged, but when spread over a larger area, the effective blur-free depth increases - or something like that. There was an earlier discussion here which came to a similar inconclusive conclusion but there was general agreement that big reflection holograms seem to have more useful depth.

posts.topic_title: New holo 8 by 10 inch made with ATI laser
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: New holo 8 by 10 inch made with ATI laser
posts.content_md: Also, I should remind the newer holographers that processing of reflection holograms greatly effects the usable depth. If you use a broadband processing scheme you get a brighter, whiter hologram but with less depth. With narrow band you get a more intense color and more depth but less brightness.

posts.topic_title: New holo 8 by 10 inch made with ATI laser
posts.author: LP
posts.post_subject: New holo 8 by 10 inch made with ATI laser
posts.content_md:
Thank you for the information. 

An effect on the brightness of the hologram is known to me by reflection-kopys. Nevertheless, there the reduction of the width affects positively the brightness. 

However, here I appealed to the Denisyuk holograms. If a narrow band promises more depth, other attempts with PFG01 will deliver (according to your information) darker results.

(What does signify this concept "broadband processing scheme "?)
